title: E0053: Unserialize without allowed_classes
plain_english: `unserialize()` can create objects of classes named inside the input. If untrusted input controls that data, it may trigger dangerous `__wakeup()` or `__destruct()` behavior in classes loaded by the application. This is commonly called object injection.
why_matters: Object injection can lead to unexpected side effects, including file writes, command execution, or other security issues, depending on which classes are available.
what_it_checks: A literal options array without an `allowed_classes` key
`allowed_classes => true`, which explicitly allows every class
